metadata.title: Boston police investigate stabbing near Northeastern University

left: A person experiencing a mental health crisis attacked a Boston police officer and an EMS worker with a sword near Northeastern University, resulting in the suspect being shot and later dying at a hospital.
Several Boston officers and EMS personnel were injured during the incident and hospitalized; all are expected to survive, according to Police Commissioner Michael Cox.
center: On Saturday, Boston Police Commissioner Michael Cox said officers fatally shot a suspect on Hemenway Street near Northeastern University following a chaotic incident involving a man armed with a sword.
Police initially responded to a 911 call at 10:44 a.m. reporting four armed individuals threatening the caller, but officers quickly determined the person was suffering from a mental health crisis.
After a 45-minute attempt to de-escalate, the man emerged and stabbed an officer in the arm, prompting officers to use Tasers and firearms. "He was armed with some type of sword," Cox said.
Several officers and the Boston EMS clinician were hospitalized with non-life-threatening injuries, while the suspect was transported to a local hospital where he later died from his wounds.
Suffolk County District Attorney Kevin Hayden announced his office is investigating the shooting, as is standard procedure for any incident involving an officer discharging their service weapon.
right: Boston Police investigated a stabbing outside 315 Huntington Street near Northeastern University where the victim fled into a university building with non-life threatening injuries and was taken to a hospital.
The suspect fled the scene and was being searched for by police, with no arrests made by midday, and the incident remains under active investigation.

sources.news_title: Man shot by police in Boston after attacking officer, EMS clinician with sword
sources.text:
Man shot by police in Boston after attacking officer, EMS clinician with sword
The suspect was experiencing a mental health episode, police said
The suspect was experiencing a mental health episode, police said
The suspect was experiencing a mental health episode, police said
A man experiencing a mental health episode was fatally shot by police after attacking an officer and an EMS clinician with a sword Saturday morning, Boston Police Commissioner Michael Cox said.
Several officers were also injured in the incident, which happened in an apartment building hallway near the Northeastern University campus.
Officers responded to 212 Hemenway St. just before 11 a.m. after receiving a 911 call about four individuals armed with a gun. The 911 caller was located by police inside an apartment building.
An EMS clinician responded to the scene and, along with police, determined that the person was suffering from a mental health episode, Cox said.
According to police, the suspect opened the apartment door after he was asked to come outside to receive help.
"He immediately opened the door and struck the clinician and an officer who was outside the door. He was armed with some type of sword, stabbing the officer in the arm and knocking the EMS clinician to the ground," Cox said. "One or more officers, which is under investigation at this time, fired a taser and weapon at the individual, bringing the person to a halt."
The suspect, EMS clinician and several officers were taken to nearby hospitals. The officer who was stabbed suffered a severe laceration. The suspect, who has not been identified, died.
"This was a very chaotic circumstance. The individual was clearly in some sort of mental distress," Suffolk County District Attorney Kevin Hayden said.
Boston EMS released a statement in response to the incident saying that one of their best clinicians was injured in the stabbing:
"Our focus tonight remains on the two members of Boston EMS, including one of our BEST clinicians, who were treated and transported to the hospital after the incident on Hemenway Street in Boston. Both suffered non-life-threatening injuries," the statement read. "Today serves as a reminder of the dangers inherent in this work and the sacrifice our members make every day. Members of Boston EMS show up to save lives — not to be assaulted. No one should face violence for simply doing their job. Our thoughts are with our injured members, the Boston Police officers, and everyone affected by today’s incident."
Northeastern University sent out an alert to students reporting police activity at 212 Hemenway St., but stated that there was no active threat to the campus.
Fenway at Forsyth Way and Huntington Avenue at Forsyth Way to Westland Avenue is closed as police investigate. Drivers and pedestrians have been asked to avoid the area.
Police do not believe the incident was connected to a recent stabbing near the Northeastern University campus.

sources.news_title: Boston officer stabbed, suspect shot dead during mental health crisis response
sources.text:
Legal
Boston officer stabbed, suspect shot dead during mental health crisis response
A Boston police officer was stabbed and the suspect was shot dead after officers, EMS and a clinician responded to an apartment for a reported mental health crisis, officials said. Several other first responders were also injured.
The incident happened at about 10:44 a.m. Saturday in the 200 block of Hemenway Street, near Northeastern University, after a man called 911 and said four people with a gun were trying to harm him, Boston Police Commissioner Michael Cox said in a press briefing.
Cox said officers found the caller inside the apartment and began speaking with him through the door. EMS and a clinician were called to the scene, and after an extended period of time they concluded the man was in immediate need of attention because he appeared to be suffering from a mental health crisis.
As responders tried to get him to come out and seek treatment, the man opened the door and attacked them, Cox said. He was armed with some type of sword and stabbed one officer in the arm, while also knocking the EMS clinician to the ground.
One or more officers then used a Taser and fired their weapons, Cox said. The man was given medical aid at the scene and taken to a hospital, where he later died.
Police applied a tourniquet to the wounded officer before he was taken to a hospital for treatment for a severe laceration. Multiple officers and the EMS clinician were also taken to local hospitals with injuries that were believed to be non-life-threatening.
Suffolk County District Attorney Kevin Hayden said his office is conducting a full investigation into the officer-involved shooting.
“This was a very chaotic circumstance,” Hayden said. “There were a number of first responders, both from the mental health perspective, as well as members of the Boston Police Department, doing everything they could to deal with a difficult situation and the individual who was clearly in some sort of mental distress.”
Hayden said investigators were still in the early stages of the case and that it would take time before authorities have a full picture of what happened.

sources.news_title: Man attacks Boston police, EMS with sword near Northeastern University, is shot and killed
sources.text:
BOSTON — A person clearly suffering from a mental health crisis attacked a police officer with a sword and was Tasered and shot, leading to his death, authorities say.
“This was a very chaotic circumstance for a number of first responders, both from the mental health perspective, as well as members of the Boston Police Department doing everything they could to deal with a difficult situation and an individual who was clearly in some sort of mental distress,” Suffolk District Attorney Kevin Hayden said at a press conference near where the incident took place.
The “chaotic” scene unfolded in the hallway of an apartment building in the 200 block of Hemenway Street in the area of Northeastern University housing late Saturday morning, authorities said.
It all began with a 10:44 a.m. 911 call in which the caller reported that four people armed with guns were after him. Police arrived and located the caller and spoke with him through the apartment door, according to Boston Police Commissioner Michael Cox.
The police quickly determined that an EMS mental health clinician would be needed because the person was “suffering some type of mental health crisis,” Cox said. The clinician, with officers present, spoke with the person through the apartment door for maybe 35 to 45 minutes.
“As they asked the individual to begin the process of maybe coming up and seeking the attention they needed, the individual immediately opened the door and struck both the clinician and an officer who was outside the door,” Cox said.
The person was armed with “some type of sword,” Cox said, and stabbed an officer with it and knocked the clinician to the ground. Cox and Hayden said that “multiple” officers were taken to hospitals, but other than the stabbed officer it is not immediately clear how the other officers were injured.
At least one officer then fired both Tasers and service pistols at the attacker, “bringing the person to a halt,” Cox said. That person was provided immediate first aid and rushed to a hospital but died from his injuries.
Cox said that department policy involving shootings is “based on the individual and the threat that’s involved,” but that initial information suggests that the “use of the firearm was properly justified in this case.”
Hayden said that with all shootings involving police, the case will be investigated by his office.
“I think it’s going to be quite some time before we’re going to be able to have a full picture of exactly what happened here,” Hayden said, “but our first responders, all of them, I think responded to the scene the best they can.”

A person experiencing a mental health crisis was fatally shot by police after attacking an officer and an EMS clinician on Saturday, Boston Police Commissioner Michael Cox said.
Police responded to an emergency call at an apartment on Hemenway Street near Northeastern University on Saturday morning.
After officers spoke to the person for a length of time, “the individual immediately opened the door. He was armed with some type of sword, stabbing the officer in the arm and knocking the EMS clinician to the ground,” Cox said.
“One or more officers fired a Taser and their firearm at the individual, bringing the person to a halt,” the commissioner said. “EMS immediately provided medical attention. Unfortunately, the person succumbed to the injuries.”

Several officers were injured in the incident, but none of their injuries are life-threatening, Cox said.
“This was a very chaotic circumstance,” Suffolk County District Attorney Kevin Hayden said. “A number of first responders — from a mental health perspective as well as members of the Boston Police Department — were doing everything they could dealing with a difficult situation.”

sources.news_title: Boston Police Fatally Shoot Sword-Wielding Suspect
sources.text:
Boston, Massachusetts — Police fatally shot an individual armed with a sword Saturday after authorities say the person attacked officers and an emergency medical clinician during a response to a reported mental health incident.
Boston Police Commissioner Michael Cox said officers were called to a residence on Hemenway Street around midday, where the individual was initially behind a door while responders attempted to assess the situation. During the interaction, the person suddenly emerged and struck an EMS clinician before stabbing a police officer in the arm.
Officers responded by deploying a Taser and then firing their weapons, stopping the attack. The individual was transported to a hospital but later died from their injuries. Authorities have not released the person’s identity.
The injured officer suffered a severe laceration and was taken to a hospital for treatment. Additional officers and the EMS clinician were also hospitalized with non-life-threatening injuries.
Officials indicated the situation involved a mental health crisis, though further details have not been disclosed. The incident remains under investigation.

sources.text:
Northeastern University shooting update: Boston police officers injured; first info on suspect
Multiple Boston police officers were taken to the hospital on Saturday after a shooting incident on Hemenway Street
Multiple Boston police officers were taken to the hospital on Saturday after a shooting incident on Hemenway Street, near Northeastern University, local media outlets reported. Steve Cooper of 7News reported that one officer suffered a stab wound. However, most of the injuries have been described as non-life threatening. The incident occurred at around 12 PM local time.
First info on suspect
Reports further stated that the suspect has been shot and has been taken to the hospital. The shooter has not been identified yet.

“Boston Update: suspect shot in officer involved shooting on Hemenway St this morning suffered critical injuries…several police officers were transported to the hospital with one officer suffering a stab wound…injuries to officers are described as non life threatening #7News,” Cooper wrote on X, platform formerly known as Twitter.
Where did the shooting take place?
Hemenway Street is a residential street located right in the heart of Northeastern University’s campus in Boston. Address: Hemenway Street, Boston, MA 02115
The street runs parallel to Huntington Avenue (the main campus artery) and is situated in the Fenway neighborhood, just west of the main academic quad. Northeastern owns and operates several residence halls directly on or facing Hemenway Street, including: 153 Hemenway Street (Loftman Hall / part of the M1LK complex), 144 Hemenway Street, 115 & 119 Hemenway Street (Kennedy Hall), 129 Hemenway Street (Smith Hall).
Read More: Is Trump Jr. eyeing White House ballroom for wedding with Bettina Anderson?
Hemenway Street is primarily a student residential area with Northeastern University housing buildings.
Several incidents near Northeastern University
Only days ago, Northeastern University officials reassured students and staff that there is no ongoing threat to campus safety following two violent incidents reported near the Boston campus.
“Our campus is safe at this time,” Ruben Galindo, Northeastern University’s chief of police, told Northeastern Global News. “There is no threat or concern.”
The incidents, both stabbings, were unrelated. Authorities described them as “random acts of violence” and emphasized there is no evidence the university or its community was specifically targeted.
University police are continuing to work closely with local authorities as the investigation unfolds. “We’re in constant communication with the Boston Police Department, assisting with information, including camera footage, to help with the investigation and apprehension of the suspects,” Galindo said.
In response, Northeastern has also stepped up its security presence. “We also have 24/7 police patrols on campus and have increased patrols since last Friday for visibility and deterrence,” he said.

sources.news_title: Stabbing victim found in Northeastern University dorm
sources.text:
Boston Police were searching for a suspect after a stabbing victim fled into a Northeastern dorm Wednesday morning, according to police.
At about 8:19 a.m., police responded to 291 Saint Botolph St., in the South End — listed by Northeastern as an East Village housing building — on a report of a person stabbed.
The victim was found at the site with “non-life threatening” injuries and taken to a local hospital, BPD said.
The original incident occurred outside of 315 Huntington St. nearby, police stated.
“A person who is not affiliated with Northeastern was injured in the incident and entered a Northeastern building where NUPD rendered aid,” said Northeastern Vice President for Communications Renata Nyul. “Although the incident did not take place on Northeastern’s campus, the university alerted its community to avoid the area while BPD and NUPD were responding.”
Police were searching for the suspect who “fled the area,” Nyul said. The Northeastern building had been fully reopened as of Wednesday afternoon.
No arrests were made, Boston Police said around noon, and the incident remained under active investigation.

sources.news_title: Person stabbed near Northeastern University; police searching for assailant - The Boston Globe
sources.text:
A person was stabbed near the campus of Northeastern University on Wednesday morning, officials said.
Around 8:19 a.m., police went to the area of 291 Saint Botolph St. in response to a report of a person stabbed, Officer Michael Torigian said.
The assault happened near the corner of Huntington Avenue and Gainsborough Street, said Renata Nyul, a university spokesperson.
The victim is not affiliated with the university, Nyul said. The person went inside a university building, where campus police provided aid, Nyul said.
The person was taken to a hospital with injuries that were not life-threatening, police said.
The university alerted its community to avoid the area while police were responding, Nyul said.
Police are searching for the assailant, who fled the area.
Around 10:30 p.m. on Friday, a Northeastern student was stabbed outside the Marino Recreation Center on Huntington Avenue, university police said.
Hannah Goeke can be reached at hannah.goeke@globe.com.

sources.news_title: Person stabbed near Northeastern University campus
sources.text:
Suspect arrested in stabbing near Northeastern University, BPD says
Police have arrested a suspect in a stabbing near the Northeastern University campus, Boston police confirmed to NewsCenter 5.
At approximately 8:15 a.m. Wednesday, an assault took place near the corner of Huntington Avenue and Gainsborough Street, according to a Northeastern spokesperson. The assailant fled.
"They were coming down Gainsborough here, just absolutely booking it, and then hung a really sharp right, and went on the other side of this building," said Lawrence Hall, a Northeastern student.
Northeastern officials said the victim ran into East Village, a building with dorms and classrooms.
"I had just left the building that they had run into, and my reaction immediately was just kind of fear. I was nervous about people I know in the building," said Allison Jenks, a freshman.
"I was just scared, I was hoping everyone there was OK I couldn't go back to my dorm, I got in touch with my roommate to make sure she wasn't hurt," said Elizabeth Harrison, another freshman.
Northeastern officials said their officers rendered first aid to the victim while Boston police investigated a second scene around the corner.
"I heard the person got aid from the campus. I'm glad that happened, I hope they're OK," said David Liu, a Northeastern graduate student.
The incident is the second violent attack in days. In a separate case, police said a Northeastern student was assaulted around the corner from the campus.
"There were no details on it, and I didn't hear anything else about it except for that. There's just weird stuff going on," said Devon Anderson.
Although the incident did not take place on Northeastern’s campus, the university alerted its community to avoid the area while Boston police and NUPD responded.
The victim is not affiliated with the school.
The suspect's identity has not been revealed.

BOSTON (WHDH) - A man has been arrested in connection with a stabbing in Boston that triggered an emergency alert at Northeastern University Wednesday morning, Boston police said.

Police said two men got into a fight at approximately 8:15 a.m. at Symphony Market on Huntington Avenue, and one pulled out a knife and stabbed the victim. The person with the knife then took off in an unknown direction.

Northeastern students received an alert, warning them to steer clear of the building on 291 Botolph Street as officers searched for the attacker. Students attend classes in the basement of that building on campus.
Students said they are concerned because they heard of another stabbing incident in the area less than a week ago.
“There can be an instance, where there is a one off stabbing. That’s something in a big urban area – but having two in the same five days is kinda crazy. And the fact that classes haven’t been canceled and there’s no, like – you don’t see a ton of police walking around at all time has to be a little bit concerning,” Higgins said.

sources.news_title: BREAKING: Suspect shot, multiple officers injured in incident on Hemenway Street – The Huntington News
sources.text:
One suspect was shot and multiple police officers were injured in an incident Saturday morning at 212 Hemenway St., according to Boston police.
Dozens of officers from the Boston Police Department, or BPD, and the Northeastern University Police Department, or NUPD, responded to the incident at about 11:40 a.m. The incident marks the third alleged assault on or near Northeastern’s Boston campus in the past eight days.
In a 12:28 p.m. email to The Huntington News, Officer Michael Torigian of the Boston Police Department’s Office of Media Relations said the incident involved a code 303, denoting a use of deadly force or use of a firearm deemed necessary for de-escalation.
Torigian told The News the injured suspect and officers were transported to separate hospitals. As of publication, the suspect and officers’ conditions are unknown.
At 11:57 a.m., Northeastern sent an urgent NU alert to the Boston campus community warning of “police activity” in the area of 212 Hemenway St.. The alert stated there is “no active threat to campus” and instructed students to avoid the scene.
On March 27, a student was stabbed outside of Marino Recreation Center. The morning of April 1, a person unaffiliated with Northeastern was stabbed near East Village, and there were reports of shots fired on Gainsborough Street that evening.
This story is developing.

Police arrested a suspect in the stabbing near East Village Wednesday morning in the area of Huntington Avenue, officials announced Wednesday evening.
The investigation update from the Boston Police Department, or BPD, said officers worked with the Northeastern University Police Department to locate the suspect using video footage. The 316 Huntington Ave. building houses the YMCA, as well as Hastings Hall.
The investigation update stated the initial incident occurred outside of 291 Huntington Ave., but the victim was located on St. Botolph Street, where East Village is located.
The suspect is expected to be arraigned for assault and battery with a dangerous weapon in Boston Municipal Court.
Updated Wednesday, April 1 at 11:45 a.m.
Police responded to a report of a person stabbed near Northeastern’s East Village Residence Hall around 8:19 a.m. Wednesday morning, according to the Boston Police Department, or BPD.
Boston Police responded to 219 Saint Bolotoph St. at approximately 8:19 a.m., and the victim was taken to a nearby hospital with non-life-threatening injuries, according to Officer Michael Torigian of the Boston Police Department’s Office of Media Relations. The Northeastern University Police Department, or NUPD, sent out an NU Alert, a email sent through the university’s emergency notification system, at 9:04 a.m. Wednesday, reporting police activity at East Village.
“At approximately 8:15 am this morning, an assault took place near the corner of Huntington Avenue and Gainsborough Street,” Renata Nyul, vice president for communications at Northeastern, said in a statement to The Huntington News. “A person who is not affiliated with Northeastern was injured in the incident and entered a Northeastern building where NUPD rendered aid. Although the incident did not take place on Northeastern’s campus, the university alerted its community to avoid the area while BPD and NUPD were responding. BPD is searching for the suspect who fled the area. The building has fully reopened.”
No arrests have been made, and the investigation remains active. This is the second report of an assault nearby since Friday night, when a student was allegedly assaulted outside Marino Recreation Center.
At 10:15 a.m., NUPD sent a follow up NU Alert notifying the community that police cleared the scene. NUPD sent a Timely Warning notification at 11:06 a.m. including the above statement.
Seneca Weiss, a first-year criminology and criminal justice combined major and resident of East Village, or EV, said she woke up to an email alert about police activity at the residence hall.
“I don’t feel safe in East Village,” she said.
Weiss said that after the incident at Marino Recreation Center March 27, she has felt less safe on campus.
“I feel like I always think of EV as really safe, but ever since the Marino incident, I feel like we’ve already been on edge, and now this is happening in my own dorm,” she said.
This story is developing.
News staff Dylan Kim contributed reporting.

sources.news_title: Man Arrested After Stabbing Near Northeastern University, Boston Police Said
sources.text:
Una persona fue trasladada al hospital tras ser apuñalada el miércoles por la mañana en Boston, cerca del campus de la Universidad Northeastern.
La policía de Boston informó que acudió, junto con la policía de la Universidad Northeastern, a un reporte de apuñalamiento alrededor de las 8:19 a.m., y que una víctima fue trasladada desde el número 291 de la calle Saint Botolph al Centro Médico Beth Israel Deaconess con heridas que no ponen en peligro su vida.
Noticias Noreste 24/7 en Telemundo Nueva Inglaterra.
La víctima sufrió laceraciones en el cuello y en el antebrazo izquierdo, según el informe policial.
La policía de Boston comunicó el miércoles por la tarde que Stephen Dantzler, de 58 años y residente de Boston, había sido arrestado bajo el cargo de agresión con arma peligrosa.
El incidente original ocurrió en el exterior del número 315 de Huntington Avenue; sin embargo, la policía indicó que la víctima fue localizada en la calle Saint Botolph, en el edificio Hastings Hall de Northeastern.
Según el informe policial, la víctima declaró que su agresor era un hombre y que ambos habían sostenido una discusión verbal dentro del establecimiento Symphony Market, en Huntington Avenue. Tras salir de la tienda, la víctima relató que la discusión se tornó física y que el sospechoso esgrimió un cuchillo, con el cual le provocó cortes en el cuello y en el antebrazo izquierdo.
La víctima contó que se dirigió a la YMCA para tratar sus heridas y que, tras encontrar el baño cerrado con llave, se dirigió hacia Hastings Hall.
Las imágenes de video mostraban dos patrullas de la policía de la Universidad Northeastern estacionadas frente a Hastings Hall. También había un vehículo de la policía de Boston estacionado frente a la cercana YMCA del Gran Boston, en Huntington Avenue, y al menos cinco patrullas de la policía de Boston estacionadas a lo largo de Huntington Avenue, cerca de la intersección con la calle Gainsborough.
La vicepresidenta de comunicaciones de Northeastern, Renata Nyul, declaró a NBC10 Boston que se produjo una agresión alrededor de las 8:15 a.m. cerca de la esquina de Huntington Avenue y la calle Gainsborough.
La persona que resultó herida en el incidente no tiene vínculos con la universidad, señaló Nyul; no obstante, ingresó en Hastings Hall posteriormente, donde recibió asistencia por parte de la policía del campus.
Aunque el incidente no tuvo lugar dentro del campus de Northeastern, Nyul indicó que la universidad alertó a su comunidad para que evitara la zona mientras las policías de Boston y de la universidad respondían a la emergencia. Desde entonces, el edificio ha reabierto sus puertas por completo.
Se espera que Dantzler comparezca ante el Tribunal Municipal de Boston para su lectura de cargos, informó la policía, aunque no precisaron cuándo tendría lugar dicha comparecencia judicial. No quedó claro de inmediato si tenía abogado.
